log_normalise is now robust_normalise(log1p(field)) - a true log stretch with the low anchor at the field minimum and the high at its 99.5th percentile, replacing the log1p(9*field/p99.5) form that was still near-linear over the bottom 99 percent. On a log-uniform field spanning six decades the quantiles now land within 0.05 of uniform (p25 0.214, p50 0.476, p75 0.741) instead of being 470x and 22x below their linear counterparts. test_log_normalise_lifts_the_body_of_a_heavy_tail is replaced by test_log_normalise_maps_a_log_uniform_field_onto_a_near_uniform_range, which pins the near-uniform contract, plus a scale-insensitivity test. Effect on the 1024^2 baseline: flow on dry ground went from p50 0.021 / p99 0.288 / max 0.54 to p50 0.384 / p99 0.714 / max 0.819. Noted in docs/erosion_baseline.md that this leaves flow and wetness bright at the median - that is the drainage area an MFD hillslope cell genuinely carries, and any cosmetic gamma belongs in terrain.preview.

Replaced the Planchon-Darboux epsilon ladder with an explicit routing potential. fill_depressions now solves the epsilon-free minimax fill, so a filled lake is one exact surface; the new flat_gradient then builds the potential over every surface the fill left flat: 2*(cells to the nearest spill) + (cells from the nearest wall, inverted), a four-neighbour geodesic count each way. flow_accumulation reads that potential for the flat cells' MFD drops instead of height differences, which is the point - the epsilon ladder's steps were about 17 float32 ulps at a plateau height of 0.5, so rounding collapsed the multiple-flow split into single-direction chains and drew the dead-straight beams and right-angle staircases. The potential's steps are integers, so the split survives and drainage fans across the lake. Verified on out/terrain/erosion-baseline/channel_flow.png at 1024^2: the beams and right angles are gone, replaced by a broad curved fan into the spill. Faint axis-aligned banding remains on the widest lake surfaces and every cell carrying it is submerged; recorded in docs/erosion_baseline.md. A Euclidean chamfer count was tried and is worse - round contours sharpen the descent into single straight rays along the distance field's medial axis. New tests: no flat cell is left without an outflow (checked on real 1024^2 and 2048^2 maps too, zero stuck cells), flat steps stay at or above 1.0, over half of flat cells split flow to two or more neighbours, the lake surface is exactly constant, and the coarse-to-fine fill equals the single-level solve. WaterParams.fill_epsilon is gone.

Fixed with a smoothed rim-lowering breach pass: terrain/channels.py:breach_depressions, called from TerrainSession.erode() right after the pipe-model sim. Groups every fill_depressions-flagged pit cell by its (exactly-constant per lake) filled value, finds the true minimum height of dry ground each lake's shore borders (torch.unique + scatter_reduce, one pass over the map, no per-basin loop), writes that target into the height field and box-blurs it, then clamps with torch.minimum against the current height so the blur only ever lowers real terrain. Repeated for a small fixed number of rounds (default 3).

The blur specifically fixes a staircase artifact: a hard cutover to the target reproduces the exact axis-aligned 4-connected artifact already fixed once for flat_gradient (af-l90.5), except baked into real exported elevation instead of a routing potential. Two harder approaches were tried and rejected first - rim-only carving converged to almost no improvement, and broad multi-hop carving silently re-leveled 96% of the map by 100+m mean change while looking severely blocky. Both parameter-tuning levers the ticket suggested (evaporation/deep-water-depth, dissolve/deposition skew) were also tested empirically and don't work - see the issue notes for full numbers.

This is a real, meaningful, but partial fix by design - `rounds` trades basin coverage against terrain detail, and a true endorheic basin (enclosed by higher ground on every side, or nested behind a second divide) is correctly left alone rather than breached. terrain/splat.py: Layer gains variation (strength, 0-1, default 0) and variation_m (macro feature size in metres, default 600, range [32, 4096]), parsed from optional [layer.<name>] keys and validated at load. weights() multiplies each layer's raw weight by 1 + variation*(2*field-1) before stacking, where field is a per-layer warped fBm (synth.warped_fbm, 3 octaves, seeded via cfg.derive_seed on a label unique to the layer name so different layers decorrelate) evaluated over channels.cfg - this keeps the multiplier centred on 1 (no bias to mean weight) and non-negative for variation<=1, and requires a ChannelStack (or anything exposing .cfg); weights() raises SplatRuleError by name if a layer sets variation but the stack has none. variation=0 is a strict no-op, verified bit-for-bit. 6 new tests in test_splat_pack.py (no-op at zero, perturbation at one, determinism, per-layer decorrelation, missing-cfg error) plus 4 in test_biomes.py (TOML round trip, defaults, out-of-range rejection).

terrain/preview.py: compose_splat_composite(weights, palette) maps a blended [H,W,L] splat.blend() output onto one flat colour per layer (SPLAT_PALETTE, 8 entries, cycling by index % len for biomes with more layers) via a weighted matmul against the palette table - directly legible per-pixel layer dominance, no per-layer alpha compositing needed since weights already sum to 1. render_splat_composite/splat_composite_preview follow the existing render_*/​*_preview split (write full-res PNG, then budget.deliver a capped view), taking either an explicit path or cfg.out_dir()/SPLAT_NAME. coverage_table(coverage) formats splat.coverage()'s tuple of per-layer dicts (duck-typed, no import of terrain.splat) into a fixed-width layer/material/mean%/dominant% table for the agent to read directly. 9 new tests in test_preview.py: hand-computed 2-layer pixel colours, palette cycling past 8 layers, bad-shape rejection, PNG write and default out_dir, budget compliance, and a hand-computed coverage table.

Resolved as part of af-hmt: biomes/temperate.toml's riverbed_gravel and silt_flat weights (smoothstep(flow, 0.55, 0.75) and smoothstep(deposition, 0.5, 0.85) * (1 - smoothstep(flow, 0.55, 0.8))) are set directly against the dry_ground quantiles in docs/erosion_baseline.md/erosion_baseline.json (flow p50 0.384/p90 0.564/p99 0.714), not hand-tuned magic numbers - the 0.55 ramp start sits right at p90 and 0.75-0.8 sits past p99, so only the upper tail of dry-ground flow lights up. Checked on a real 256^2 continental terrain, restricted to water<0.5 cells (79.7% of the map): riverbed_gravel is dominant on 6.5% of dry ground, silt_flat on 4.2% - a believable riverbank/gravel-bar minority, neither the 'selects nothing' failure this bug described nor the 'selects most of the map' risk the notes flagged for a low median-adjacent threshold.

terrain/scatter.py: density_rock (wear + bedrock exposure), density_tree (moisture x gentle slope, set back from the shore by a real dilate()-based buffer in metres, not an approximated one), density_grass (takes the caller's pre-summed biome grass-layer weight - scatter.py has no biome-specific layer names - thinned on slope) and density_debris (deposition pooling OR a flow-gradient edge detector, for the discontinuity at a channel's bank). All four multiply through a shared _avoid() term - (1-water) x (1-channel_bed) x (1-steep) - built from the water channel directly (never approximated from flow) plus a flow-magnitude channel-bed term and a slope-steepness term, so every mask visibly avoids open water, channel beds and sheer rock as the bug required. ScatterParams holds every threshold, validated low<high at construction. build()/quantise()/write()/coverage() follow splat.py's pack/write/coverage shape: write() emits the 4 fixed 8-bit grayscale PNGs CLAUDE.md names (scatter_rock/tree/grass/debris.png). 17 tests in tests/test_scatter.py using a synthetic 4-quadrant stack (open water / channel bed / steep rock / safe) for exact hand-computed assertions, plus a dedicated water-buffer distance test and ScatterParams range-rejection cases. game_ready_pass(objects, atlas_size=2048, material_name="atlas_material"):
- applies transforms and recalculates normals per object (reuses assets.hardsurface.apply_transforms/recalc_normals)
- set_origin_to_base_centre: computes the combined world bbox of the whole group, moves every object's own origin to that shared base-centre point via the 3D cursor, then relocates the group to world (0,0,0) - satisfies validate_asset's origin-at-base-centre world-bbox check for both single- and multi-object assets
- uv_unwrap_and_pack: smart-UV-projects each object individually, then multi-object-edit-mode pack_islands packs every island from every object into one shared 0-1 atlas layout
- consolidate_material: clears every material slot on every object and assigns one shared atlas material, so every polygon points at material_index 0
- enforce_power_of_two_textures: walks the atlas material's image texture nodes and scales any non-power-of-two image up to the next power of two, capped at atlas_size (a no-op today since af-4ir.1 texture baking hasn't landed yet - this is the plumbing it will hit)

generate_lods(lod0, ratios=(1.0, 0.5, 0.15), normal_map_size=1024):
- lod0 is renamed with a _LOD0 suffix and used as-is (must already have a material from game_ready_pass)
- LOD1/2 are duplicates of LOD0 reduced with a Decimate (COLLAPSE) modifier at ratios[1]/ratios[2] - UVs come along for free via the modifier's own vertex interpolation, never re-unwrapped, so "keep UVs shared" means literally inherited, not regenerated
- bake_normal_map bakes LOD0's surface normal onto each reduced LOD's own UVs via Cycles selected-to-active (cage_extrusion scaled off LOD0's bbox diagonal so the ray cast clears the decimated surface), into a fresh Image per LOD, wired through a ShaderNodeNormalMap into a *copy* of the shared atlas material's Principled BSDF Normal input - so LOD1/2 keep every other channel (albedo, ORM) identical to the one shared atlas material and only the normal map input differs per LOD, matching "keep ... material shared" for everything but the thing that has to differ per LOD by construction
- returns LodSet(objects, triangle_counts, normal_maps) - triangle_counts lets a caller assert the ratios landed; normal_maps names the baked Image per LOD (None for LOD0)

Alpine needed a colder test terrain than any existing one: temperature = f(height) is calibrated around a 22C sea-level baseline, so a normal terrain (e.g. "gate", height_range_m 900) never drops below ~0.62 normalized and every cold-gated layer reads 0%. Built out/terrain/alpine_test (1024^2, highland shape, height_range_m 5200, seed 4242) to get a real freezing zone (temperature 0.234-0.704, mean 0.498) and slope up to 0.95 (mean 0.46 - a genuinely rugged terrain). First pass had exposed_rock eating 75% of the map because its slope gate and the vegetation slope gate weren't complementary (a 0.28-0.4 slope gap fell through to nothing, silent_fraction 0.33, defaulting to layer 0) and its temperature gate saturated almost everywhere since the crossover wasn't centred on this terrain's actual median temperature. Fixed by making every slope-based split use the same two edges on both sides (smoothstep(slope,a,b) and its complement 1-smoothstep(slope,a,b) sum to exactly 1, so there is no gap) and recentring the rock/scree temperature crossover on the terrain's real median (0.4-0.56, not a guessed absolute). Final coverage: glacial_wash 2.96%, glacial_silt 10.48%, tundra_turf 9.64%, alpine_meadow 6.94%, talus_scree 28.26%, exposed_rock 39.65%, snowfield 2.06%, silent_fraction 0.0 - all under 45%, all 7 layers nonzero on a terrain built specifically to exercise the cold end of the rule set.

Fixed by replacing bpy.ops.uv.smart_project + bpy.ops.uv.pack_islands in assets/game_ready.py:uv_unwrap_and_pack with a from-scratch bmesh unwrap+pack. Root cause was worse than filed: smart_project itself collapses most islands to zero UV area on this content (verified on a bare bevelled cube, no greeble - 4/6 faces degenerate) and pack_islands cannot separate ~90+ islands without overlap at any margin/margin_method/angle_limit - the af-80b pre-triangulation fix only reduced the count because it happened to shrink island counts, never touched either root cause.

New pipeline: axis-project each face onto the plane orthogonal to its dominant normal axis+sign (never degenerates a non-degenerate 3D face), union-find faces into islands via bmesh edge adjacency gated on that axis+sign AND a live overlap check during growth (a candidate face is rejected from a group if its projected shape would overlap a shape already merged in - needed because the EXACT boolean solver leaves genuinely overlapping coplanar triangles at some cut seams, e.g. window_recess's sill ring, which axis+sign matching alone can't distinguish from a legitimate flat island), then a deterministic shelf packer places every island's bounding box with a guaranteed margin gap (no overlap possible by construction, unlike pack_islands' heuristic). Each triangle is additionally shrunk 0.5% toward its own centroid for clearance against float-noise-scale seam artifacts.

export_asset(objects, name, kind):
- export_glb writes out/assets/<name>/<name>.glb via bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf (use_selection, export_apply) - the exporter itself converts Blender's Z-up to Y-up
- walks every unique material assigned across objects, and every unique TEX_IMAGE node.image on those materials, saving each to out/assets/<name>/textures/<image>.png (image.filepath_raw + file_format="PNG" + save())
- groups objects by a trailing _LODn suffix (lod.py's generate_lods naming convention; falls back to a single "LOD0" group when absent) and sums triangle counts per group
- computes the world-space bbox (metres, since 1 Blender unit = 1m per CLAUDE.md) from matrix_world @ bound_box corners across all objects
- writes out/assets/<name>/asset.json: name, kind (validated against hero_building/prop/vehicle), glb filename, textures list, materials list, triangle_counts per LOD, bbox_min/max, and a contact_sheet path matching contact_sheet.py's SHEET_NAME convention (duplicated as a local constant rather than imported, since contact_sheet.py pulls in PIL which isn't guaranteed present in Blender's bundled Python)

Replaced the smoothed-rim breach_depressions (af-g22.8) with a proper least-cost/priority-flood-style breach in terrain/channels.py: for each closed basin, _lake_escape now finds the true lowest ground it can reach through however-thick a dry rim via a bounded multi-hop relaxation (_dry_reach, new), not just the immediate 1-hop neighbour - this fixes the "1-2 cell shoulder" gap af-g22.8 flagged. _breach_round then carves only the actual chain of dry cells the search walked through (via _geodesic from the crossing point) plus a small fixed-radius margin at the mouth, not a whole-lake-sized blur - so the lake's own floor and the rest of its rim are left untouched, and fill_depressions recomputing afterwards is what shrinks the lake correctly.

Two real bugs found and fixed during implementation, both only visible against real data, not the small synthetic unit fixtures:
1. A "no genuine improvement" case (rim borders dry ground only at exactly its own flood level, e.g. a truly enclosed bowl) was initially still producing a doorway, because multiple cells trivially tie for the group minimum when it isn't actually lower than the flood level. Fixed by gating on `resolved < own_flood_level` before treating anything as a crossing.
2. The first real-terrain validation (coastal_range, seed 20260916, 1024^2) showed the per-lake-bounded channel design breaks in aggregate: a real eroded height field carries thousands of pixel-scale noise pits, and even though each one's channel is individually bounded by reach_m, their union covered 89.6% of the map with visible staircasing - worse than the fix being replaced. Fixed with a minimum-lake-size gate (min_area_m2, default 400 m^2 in the function signature) so noise-scale pits are left alone entirely, same as a lake with no improving escape.

assets/lod.py: _decimate now protects small/thin disjoint loose parts (hinges, finials, glass panes) from the flat COLLAPSE ratio via a Decimate vertex_group built from union-find over the joined mesh's loose parts - any part whose own bbox diagonal is under 5% of the object's full diagonal is left out of the eligible group entirely, so the modifier never touches it. assets/validate.py: _check_manifold now tolerates the specific harmless pattern - a 4-valence edge where exactly two of the four incident triangles are coplanar and face exactly opposite directions (face-normal dot < -0.999). That pattern is unambiguous: two triangles sharing an edge with antiparallel normals must lie in the same plane, so together they bound zero net material and are safe to leave in place. This covers the "door frame's inner cutout matching the wall opening" case and any two solidified slabs whose rim caps end up coplanar (e.g. wall panels butting at a corner).

Implementation: replaced _edge_counts (returned bare counts, no face identity) with _edge_face_map (edge -> incident triangle indices) plus _face_normal/_is_welded_seam. _check_manifold now classifies each edge: boundary (1), fine (2), tolerated welded seam (4 with a matching antiparallel pair, reported in the detail string but does not fail the check), or non-manifold (everything else, including 4-valence edges with no matching pair, and any higher valence). Added tests/test_validate.py cases for both the tolerated and still-flagged valence-4 shapes; updated existing manifold tests to the new signature via a _manifold_checks test helper.

Explicitly NOT covered: the ridge-line case (two independently-solidified roof slopes meeting at a peak), where the two extra rim faces are NOT coplanar with each other (they point along each slope's own normal, not opposite directions) - so this fix does not relax that case, and it will still correctly fail validate_asset. Resolving that generally needs either modelling the roof as one connected shell before solidifying (so the ridge edge is never a boundary edge in the first place) or a proper angular-wedge continuity classifier, which needs empirical validation against real Blender-generated geometry to get right - left as a follow-up if it comes up in practice.
